text:
maya: quick heads-up — saw a weird output shift when pushing int8 compiled weights on long prompts (~30k tokens). starts fine, then after ~24k theres a systematic token drift (off-by-one) in the middle of generated code block :thinking:

kai: can you paste a minimal repro? is this only with the new quant pipeline or also float16? :eyes:

maya: repro attached below. float16 is fine. repro uses int8+fused-attn build.

```
# run on local dev machine (nn-serve)
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-13b-int8-fused","input":"<very long prompt>"}' > out.json
jq .out[12000:12100] out.json | sed -n '1,80p'
```

luca: interesting — sounds like a ring buffer wrap problem in the sliding attention index. did you try forcing smaller chunk_size/buffer_size? could be the circular buffer pointer overflowing the stride math.

maya: yes tried buffer=32768 and 65536, same. toggling `prefetch_kv=false` changes onset point slightly but still drift happens. i captured model logs showing `attn_idx` jumping backward by 1 around token 23987.

ci-bot: build 2026.03.18-int8-fuse completed on branch quant/fast-attn — tests: 214 passed, 5 flaky (longctx smoke).

kai: can you paste the exact log excerpt? also what rotary scaling code path are you using (legacy RoPE vs rescaled)?

maya: log snippet:

```
[2026-03-18T14:22:19Z] INFO decoder: token=23986 attn_idx=23986
[2026-03-18T14:22:20Z] INFO decoder: token=23987 attn_idx=23987
[2026-03-18T14:22:21Z] INFO decoder: token=23988 attn_idx=23987  # <-- stuck one behind
[2026-03-18T14:22:21Z] WARN decoder: ringbuf_wrap delta=-1
```

luca: delta=-1 on that path suggests pointer arithmetic borrowed from 32-bit index somewhere in compiled kernel. int truncation after quant conv maybe.

maya: good call. we built kernel with `INDEX_T=int32` for float build but int16 for int8? i will check compile flags.

kai: also check the remapping in the attention fused kernel — we had a recent change that uses `pos_mod = (pos + offset) & mask` where mask is based on `buffer_size-1`. if offset computed in 64-bit and truncated to 32-bit during IR emit, wrappoints move.

maya: minimal diff i ran: forcing INDEX_T=int64 in the fused kernel made the repro go away locally. but performance regressed ~4%.

eva: sounds like candidate for conditional cast depending on longctx flag. we shouldn't globally promote to int64 — maybe only when max_ctx > 2^31/2? also need a test in the quant CI for long runs.

luca: agree. create a small unit test that exercises ring buffer pointer arithmetic with long offsets and both int8 and float builds.

maya: creating PR with two things: 1) cast fixes guarded by MAX_CTX threshold, 2) longctx-smoke added to quant-nightly. will tag @oncall-ml for review.

kai: add a benchmark to measure the perf delta with a synthetic run so we can quantify the 4% hit and see if we can optimize cast paths.

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/4821 — includes logs, repro script, and CI job. please review.

ci-bot: PR 4821 opened by maya. CI: run quant-nightly-longctx (queued).

luca: quick question — do we want to backport to dedicated nodes that are already in prod? i think yes if the repro exists in customer traces.

maya: found one customer trace in SRE logs with symptoms (ticket #RD-3421) — flagged security & cs. leaning to backport to 2026.02-stable.

kai: +1 for backport. if we gate by MAX_CTX threshold we minimize perf impact for typical workloads.

eva: can we add telemetry metric to detect attn_idx delta != 1 in production to catch regressions early? simple counter increment when delta != 1.

maya: good idea, will add a short-lived metric `attn_ring_delta_non1_total` and an alert for rate > 1/hour per node.

luca: nice. after merge can we run a long 48h smoke on staging with int8 build and long prompts (30k tokens) to be safe.

maya: will queue long-run job on staging once CI green. thanks all :thumbsup:

kai: thanks for catching this, great writeup. 

eva: :rocket:
